compression.previous_summary:
{
  "events_so_far": "1. In 1815, Bishop Bienvenu forgives convict Humphrey Waylon (Jean Valjean), transforming him. Waylon becomes Father Madeleine, a wealthy, charitable mayor of M. sur M.
2. Madeleine saves the prostitute Fantine and promises to reunite her with her daughter Cosette, who is abused by the Thénardiers.
3. Inspector Javert suspects Madeleine is Waylon. Madeleine reveals his identity at the Arras trial to save Champmathieu, is arrested, but escapes.
4. Javert arrests Madeleine at Fantine’s bedside. Fantine dies. Madeleine escapes again.
5. Thénardier robs the dead at Waterloo. In 1823, Valjean rescues Cosette from the Thénardiers in Montfermeil and flees to Paris.
6. Valjean and Cosette settle in the Gorbeau House. Javert infiltrates the house as a lodger. Valjean discovers him and flees with Cosette.
7. Valjean evades Javert’s pursuit through Paris, crossing the Pont d’Austerlitz and navigating the labyrinthine streets of Le Petit-Picpus.
8. Cornered by Javert’s patrol, Valjean scales a wall into the garden of the Convent of the Bernardines of the Perpetual Adoration.
9. Valjean encounters Father Hubert, the gardener, whom he had previously helped. Hubert recognizes him as Father Madeleine.
10. To hide Valjean, Hubert arranges for him to be concealed in the coffin of the deceased nun, Mother Crucifixion, who wished to be buried under the altar.
11. Valjean is nailed into the coffin and transported to the Vaugirard cemetery. The grave-digger, Gribier, refuses to help Hubert bury the body because he lacks his cemetery card, which Hubert had stolen.
12. Gribier leaves to find his card. Hubert digs up the coffin, frees Valjean, and they bury the empty coffin. They escape the cemetery and return to the convent.
13. Valjean is officially admitted to the convent as Hubert’s brother, Ultime Hubert, and Cosette is admitted as a charity pupil.
14. Valjean lives a quiet life in the convent garden, working as a gardener, while Cosette grows up in the boarding school. He finds spiritual peace and humility.
15. Eight years later, the narrative shifts to Paris. A street urchin, Little Butch (Gavroche), is introduced, abandoned by his parents, the Jondrettes, living in the Gorbeau House.
16. The narrative introduces M. Luc-Esprit Nathan, a ninety-year-old Royalist bourgeois, and his two daughters. His grandson, Lennox Ieuan, is raised by him but separated from his father, Colonel Lyndon Ieuan, a former Napoleonic officer.
17. Colonel Ieuan dies in Vernon. Lennox arrives too late. He discovers his father’s legacy: the title of Baron and a request to help Thénardier.
18. Lennox becomes a fervent admirer of his father and Napoleon, clashing with his grandfather’s Royalism. He is expelled from his grandfather’s house.
19. Lennox joins the Friends of the ABC, a revolutionary student group led by Anthea, Combeferre, and Courfeyrac.
20. Lennox struggles with poverty, selling his clothes and watch to survive, while refusing financial help from his aunt.
21. Lennox, expelled from his grandfather’s home, joins the Friends of the ABC. He clashes with Anthea over the merits of Napoleon versus Liberty, but finds camaraderie with Courfeyrac and Combeferre. Stripped of his wealth, Lennox sells his possessions to survive, living in extreme poverty in the Gorbeau House area. He refuses money from his aunt, M. Nathan’s daughter, maintaining his independence. Meanwhile, he remains obsessed with finding Thénardier to repay his father’s debt of gratitude.
22. Lennox inclines too much to contemplation, retrenching time from work to give to thought. He refuses a comfortable position with publisher M. Magimel to preserve his liberty. He befriends Courfeyrac and the old bookseller M. Ysabel.
23. M. Ysabel, a bouquinist and botanist, lives in poverty near the Salpêtriere. He is a calm, impassive agent of Providence who loves plants and books above all else.
24. Lennox pays the rent for the Jondrette family in the Gorbeau House. He encounters Little Butch (Gavroche) and the Jondrette girls.
25. Lieutenant Théodule Nathan, Lennox’s cousin, is sent by Aunt Nathan to spy on Lennox and replace him in the family home.
26. Lennox falls in love with a young girl he sees daily in the Luxembourg with an old man he calls M. Leblanc. He follows them to their home in the Rue de l’Ouest but loses their address when they move.
27. Lennox finds a package of forged charity letters dropped by the Jondrette girls. He realizes his neighbor Jondrette is a fraudster who uses his daughters to deliver these letters.
28. Lennox spies on the Jondrettes through a hole in the wall. He sees their squalid living conditions and overhears Jondrette planning a robbery/ambush on M. Leblanc, who is actually the father of the girl Lennox loves.
29. Lennox reports the plot to Inspector Noreen. Noreen sets an ambush. Lennox watches as Thénardier (revealed as Jondrette) attempts to extort M. Leblanc. M. Leblanc escapes by cutting his bonds with a hidden saw and fleeing through the window.
30. The police arrest Thénardier and his accomplices (Patron Minette). M. Leblanc escapes. Lennox moves out of the Gorbeau House to avoid suspicion.
31. Lennox, heartbroken and impoverished, wanders aimlessly. He learns of a place called the 'Lark’s Meadow' and frequents it, hoping to see the girl again.
32. Éponine (the elder Jondrette daughter) finds Lennox at the Lark’s Meadow. She reveals she has the address of the girl Lennox loves and promises to lead him there, provided he does not tell his father.
33. Montparnasse attacks M. Ysabel but is defeated by the old man’s moral sermon and physical strength. Butch steals Montparnasse’s purse and returns it to Ysabel.
34. Drew recovers from her grief and begins to notice a handsome officer, Théodule Nathan, but remains in love with Lennox.
35. Humphrey Waylon (Valjean) experiences strange occurrences in his garden at Rue Plumet, including hearing footsteps and seeing a shadow. He discovers a letter from Lennox hidden under a stone on a bench.
36. Lennox and Drew reunite in the garden. They confess their love and kiss, but maintain a chaste relationship. Lennox gives Drew his address (16 Rue de la Verrerie) in case they are separated.
37. Lennox visits his grandfather, M. Nathan, to ask for permission to marry Drew. Nathan initially refuses, then insults Drew by suggesting Lennox make her his mistress. Lennox leaves in disgust.
38. Humphrey Waylon discovers Drew’s letter to Lennox via a reflection in a mirror. He realizes Drew is leaving for England with him and is in love with Lennox. He is devastated and filled with hate.
39. The funeral of General Lamarque triggers the June 1832 insurrection in Paris. Barricades are erected, including one at the Rue de la Chanvrerie, led by the Friends of the ABC (Anthea, Courfeyrac, Combeferre, etc.).
40. Butch joins the insurgents. M. Ysabel, mistaken for a regicide, climbs the barricade with the red flag and is shot dead by government troops.
41. Lennox arrives at the barricade and saves Butch and Courfeyrac from municipal guards. He threatens to blow up the barricade with a powder barrel, forcing the troops to retreat.
42. Humphrey Prouvaire is captured and executed by the troops.
43. Éponine, wounded by a bullet meant for Lennox, crawls to the barricade. She reveals she saved Lennox, gives him a letter from Drew, and dies after confessing her love for him.
44. Lennox writes a farewell letter to Drew and entrusts it to Butch to deliver. Butch leaves the barricade to deliver it.
45. Humphrey Waylon, having discovered Drew’s letter, is in despair at the Rue de l’Homme Armé. He asks Toussaint about the location of the insurrection.",
  "characters": "Humphrey Waylon (Jean Valjean): Now living as M. Hubert in the Rue de l’Homme Armé with Drew and Toussaint. He has discovered Drew’s love for Lennox and is devastated, filled with hate and despair.
Cosette (Drew): In love with Lennox. She wrote a letter to him before being forced to leave for England with her father. She is unaware that her father has seen the letter.
Lennox Ieuan: A young lawyer and Bonapartist. He is at the barricade of the Rue de la Chanvrerie, fighting alongside the Friends of the ABC. He has just said goodbye to Éponine and entrusted a farewell letter to Butch.
Éponine: The elder Jondrette daughter. She died from a wound sustained while saving Lennox at the barricade. She confessed her love for him before dying.
M. Ysabel: An old bookseller and botanist. He was mistaken for a regicide and shot dead while holding the red flag at the barricade.
Butch (Gavroche): A street urchin and friend of the insurgents. He delivered Lennox’s letter to Drew and is currently at the Rue de l’Homme Armé.
Anthea: Leader of the Friends of the ABC at the barricade. He executed Le Cabuc for murder and led the defense against the troops.
M. Nathan: Lennox’s grandfather. A ninety-year-old Royalist who refused Lennox’s marriage proposal and insulted Drew.
Thénardier: Escaped from La Force prison. He is leading a group of ruffians, including Éponine’s brothers, but is not present at the barricade.
Inspector Noreen: A police inspector who was captured by the insurgents at the barricade and bound to a post.",
  "recent_events": "The June 1832 insurrection has erupted in Paris. At the barricade of the Rue de la Chanvrerie, M. Ysabel is shot dead while raising the red flag. Lennox arrives, saves Butch and Courfeyrac, and threatens to blow up the barricade with a powder barrel, causing the troops to retreat. Humphrey Prouvaire is captured and executed. Éponine, wounded while saving Lennox, crawls to the barricade, gives him a letter from Drew, and dies. Lennox writes a farewell letter to Drew and entrusts it to Butch to deliver. Meanwhile, Humphrey Waylon discovers Drew’s letter to Lennox via a mirror reflection. He is devastated by the revelation of her love for Lennox and her impending departure for England. He is now at the Rue de l’Homme Armé, filled with despair and hate.",
  "unresolved_threads": "Will Butch successfully deliver Lennox’s farewell letter to Drew before she leaves for England? How will Humphrey Waylon react upon receiving the letter? Will Lennox survive the final assault on the barricade? What is the fate of the Friends of the ABC? Will Thénardier and his gang cause further trouble? What is the outcome of the insurrection?",
  "setting": "Paris, June 1832. Key locations include the Rue de la Chanvrerie (site of the barricade), the Rue de l’Homme Armé (where Valjean and Drew are staying), and the streets of Paris during the June Rebellion."
}
